title: Align compact form fieldsets and inline actions for screen reader and keyboard consistency
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: As we expand compact and dense UI modes across Console tables, forms, and inline action groups, several teams reported inconsistent keyboard behaviour and screen-reader announcements. This ticket focuses on harmonizing fieldset semantics, ARIA labelling, tab order, and color token contrast for inline buttons and inputs so compact mode matches the default accessibility baseline.

Scope:
- Audit compact form fieldsets, inline action groups inside table rows, and compact button variants for ARIA roles and tab order.
- Normalize usage of legend, aria-labelledby / aria-describedby patterns for grouped form controls.
- Ensure focus order and visible focus ring persist in compact mode and when density tokens reduce padding.
- Fix contrast regressions introduced by token compressions for critical action buttons and table inline controls.
- Produce VPAT evidence pages and accessibility test matrix for QA and compliance teams.

Out of scope: full refactor of data-table keyboard model (separate epic).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Screen reader announces group labels reliably for at least 90% of compact form examples in the component library.
2) Tab order is logical and consistent: inputs -> inline actions -> next row.
3) Focus ring and hit target meet WCAG 2.1 AA patterns for keyboard users at compact density.
4) Contrast checks pass automated scans (WCAG AA) for primary/critical buttons in compact view.
5) VPAT fragment and test artifacts submitted to Compliance folder and linked in this ticket.

Proposed solution:
- Introduce a compact-fieldset token set that maps legend font-size and spacing while preserving accessible names.
- Add role="group" with aria-labelledby reference where fieldset/legend are not viable (table row inlines).
- Update compact button token variants to retain accessible contrast by bumping background or swapping text tokens for critical importance actions.
- Create a design spec and a small component-level test harness (storybook instance) that exposes keyboard navigation scenarios for QA.

Design artifacts and references:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/design-system-compact-a11y (see pages: Compact Forms, Inline Actions)
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/Compact+Fieldset+Accessibility+Spec
- VPAT template (Compliance): https://drive.redwood.com/VPAT/2026/compact-fieldsets-vpat-draft.docx
- Storybook test harness branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-components/pull/1987

Rollout plan:
1) Merge small token changes behind feature flag in design-system package.
2) QA accessibility sweep with NVDA/VoiceOver + keyboard test matrix; capture recordings and notes.
3) Update VPAT fragment and request Compliance review.
4) Ship design-system release and monitor console-integrations for regressions (1 week guarded release).

Risks and trade-offs:
- Increasing contrast for compact buttons may slightly alter visual density; mitigation: use focused A/B with product PMs and allow opt-in token variant only for critical buttons.
- Some legacy table row markup cannot easily be converted to fieldset; we will use role="group" fallback with robust aria-labelledby references.

QA checklist (short):
- [ ] Run axe-core scans on component storybook pages (compact forms, inline actions, compact buttons).
- [ ] Manual keyboard walkthroughs: tab/shift-tab, arrow keys where applicable, ensuring tab stops are correct.
- [ ] Screen reader walkthroughs: NVDA (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS), TalkBack (Android) for representative stories.
- [ ] Contrast validation screenshots for renamed tokens.

Notes and additional context:
- Related design ticket DES-33218 contains guidance on interactive role mapping; review for patterns we can re-use.
- Engineering lead recommends small incremental token changes to limit runtime churn (ENG-7345).
